scenarios.title: Browse the /publish package list with available, one-seat-left, and fully booked packages
scenarios.intent: Prove the package comparison page shows the fixed package set, package-card features, seat-capacity messaging, and the correct action for packages with plural remaining seats, exactly one remaining seat, and no seats left.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for package and availability-state classes; bva for seat-count boundaries. expand_bva on bounds min=1 and max=6 returned authoritative variants 0, 1, 2, 5, 6, 7, which justified exercising the outcome-changing boundaries at 1 remaining seat and 0 remaining seats plus the plural class above 1. Risk-judged interaction strength was 3 because money applies, but no covering-array reduction was used here because the outcome changes by availability class, so those classes stayed explicit within one boundary journey. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained as highest value because it covers the shared-seat behavior that changes package choice across all visitors.

scenarios.title: Open each publishing package detail page and verify commercial details
scenarios.intent: Prove every real package detail page exposes its package code, tagline, price, turnaround in business days, and feature list.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp across the four real package identities; covering_array requested at strength 3 because money applies and degraded to effective strength 1 because there is only one input dimension (package). The authoritative package coverage set enumerated Starter, Standard, Premium, and Author's Choice, so this one happy-path scenario sweeps all four as equivalent-input variations without splitting them into separate outcome paths. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained because it covers the published package facts authors compare before purchase.

scenarios.title: Request a publishing package that does not exist and receive a 404 page
scenarios.intent: Prove an invalid package request returns a 404 response instead of a generic error page.
scenarios.technique_notes: Techniques: negative for the missing-resource path; eqp between existing package requests and nonexistent package requests, with the nonexistent class separated because it changes the outcome from a detail view to a 404. Budget ceiling 3 applied; this scenario was retained because the source promised a distinct failure mode that protects the package-discovery flow from generic errors.

judgements.rationale: Highest value because it covers the money-facing package-selection state changes at plural seats, singular seat, and fully booked capacity, plus the globally shared seat-pool rule that affects every author.
High value because it verifies the published commercial facts on the detail pages for every legitimate package, which authors use to compare paid options.
Moderate value because it covers the promised negative path for bad package requests and guards against a generic error page, but it affects fewer users than the main comparison flows.
